description: 631-19-002 Upgrade Steam Distribution System Phase 2 Industry Day Recap Understand Challenges for construction regarding this project from a contractor s perspective. Is there any ability to alter phasing? VA Response: In-short, yes. As a result of your inquiries the project team is proposing phasing to turn over both basement and first floor wings coordinate well in advance to close, relocate, or adjust clinical operations for a fixed period. This includes a lengthy shut down of the canteen in summer months. This will allow more day shift work, more sustained/efficient construction avoiding nightly restoration. With careful planning and temporary heat provision plans by contractor this could also permit work during heating season. The solicitation will contain an updated phasing supplement by wings with permissible down time that shall supersede any specification or drawing phasing plans. We anticipate evaluating proposals with at least 1 factor demonstrating a contractor s utilization of these updates to indicate their time and cost savings relative to off-hours work. This supplement will also include operation constraints such as audiology and pharmacy where noisy work and infection control issues will push to off hours work. When is this project going to be solicited? VA Response: The intention is for this to be solicited late quarter three or quarter four. This presents an excellent opportunity for the awardee to utilize the winter of 26/27 to procure materials, complete admin and detailed coordination drawings for building 1, while utilizing immediately available work in buildings 15 and 16 to establish team dynamics, rhythm, and process to build steam. Are there any specific needs of the facility? Can a contractor utilize temporary heaters? Can a contractor bring in an engineering team to help assist? VA Response: VA would be willing to review these proposed methods. Again, the expectation is for a best value solicitation. The VA is highly motivated to complete this critical infrastructure. We will gladly review RFIs and evaluate tradeoffs. Topics so far we would happy to entertain: Value engineering proposal to change any load to hydronic. Rough sizing calcs demonstrating heating loads are satisfied Advantages: Copper/pluming work vs schedule 80 pipe welding. Significant pipe size reduction in mains, elimination of traps and maintenance costs long term, elimination of gravity dependent pathways. Elimination of smaller condensate pumps such as PTOT, customer care suite, canteen, mech room (still one in sub-basement), elimination of canteen CP by Walk-in. Savings proposals based on phasing supplement and temp heating to allow more winter work. Proposal to include products such as dryers and low maintenance sustainment. Any proposals increasing serviceable and low maintenance sustainment or energy rebate alternative ideas could be considered under best value Rathert than working above drop ceilings propose potential ceiling replacements if phasing supplement turns over. Is there any consideration to move away from the non-destructive testing? There are potential pitfalls in utilizing this method. VA Response: VA will look at this and review the methods. The current thought process is to establish minimal surveillance or critical areas where NDT including radiation exclusion radius/sphere will be performed off hours. This will likely be a hybrid between the standard specification and more than B31.1 would typically require. It could also include requirement to document process for items like socket weld (e.g. construction photo showing insertion scribe and back off . Has the VA looked at the potential use of swing spaces? Other VA s have utilized this approach to allow large areas to be vacated in an effort to provide uninterrupted work. VA Response: The utilization of swing spaces is being explored. VA will provide an updated phasing supplement with the solicitation. Is there the ability block off more rooms at a time to avoid the need to restore rooms each day? VA Response: This could be considered. The updated phasing supplement will be provided with the solicitation. Can the Canteen be down for an extended period of time? VA Response: VA is looking into potentially shutting this down for a period of time to allow efficient work. The updated phasing supplement will be provided with the solicitation. How would the VA handle unforeseen asbestos? Is there the ability to utilize a unit price? VA Response: This could be a potential line item for the solicitation. Has the VA looked at reducing the requirement for a degreed engineer for the MEP Coordinator, or all other disciplines? VA Response: VA will take a look at the requirements, but having a qualified MEP Coordinator on this specific job is the intention. Is there the ability for an administrative NTP to be issued? This would allow for more thorough site investigations and planning. It appears that in order to do a proper investigation and coordination drawings the period would need to be longer than the one-hundred and twenty (120) days in the specifications. However, an evaluation factor with major milestones schedule and Proposed Period of Performance would be likely for this project resulting in the intent of this question and maximum flexibility for the prime contractor. The VA would greatly value any commitment that documents the bulk of the administrative data and planning before mobilizing; we believe this is best value for the government and the prime contractor. This would need to be an RFI, there are issues when schedule 80 is called for. If allowed it will likely have size limitations for condensate and smaller for LP steam. VA Response: VA would be willing to entertain alternative methods so long as they meet the requirements of the contract and specifications. Deviations or value engineering proposals deviating to above and beyond such as stainless steel can be considered pre award depending on solicitation details What if any value engineering ideas should be considered. Would the VA consider adding moisture separators into the project? description: Purpose: This is a Sources Sought. The Space Systems Command (SSC) located at Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is seeking information in the form of Statements of Capabilities (SOC) from interested parties in support of the SSC, Space Domain Awareness and Combat Power Directorate requirement for the Counter Communications System (CCS) Meadowlands as described below. The Government is conducting market research to inform its Acquisition Strategy. The purpose of this notice is to identify potential sources that can meet CFC/MD3�s requirement. The Government reserves the right to set this acquisition, or portions thereof, aside for small business � to include socially and economically disadvantaged businesses, 8(a) firms, or woman-owned businesses. The Government is seeking contractors interested in and capable of providing all technical and logistical effort required to design, develop, and deliver capabilities to support the CCS Meadowlands system. Background and Description: Scope: This effort encompasses all technical, logistical, software and hardware efforts required to produce CCS Meadowlands systems. Period and Place of Performance: It is envisioned that the period of performance will be approximately 12 months in duration. The Government is working through the details to determine when the contract will start. The place of performance is flexible to allow contractor to provide an optimized solution. Background: CCS System: CCS is a ground-based counter satellite communications (SATCOM) system specifically designed to reversibly deny, disrupt, and degrade adversarial SATCOM. The basic CCS concept is to provide a flexible, modular, scalable, rapidly deployable system with a key set of signal processing/generation (SP) capabilities, selected counter SATCOM missions, and a robust transmit capability. Its architecture will be designed to host core capabilities and/or other more sophisticated �plug and play� type modules to address the ever-increasing number of technologies and assets available to our adversaries. The latest CCS Meadowlands will have upgraded capabilities compared to the existing CCS 10.2 Systems. The future CCS Meadowlands fleet will be composed of at least 32 systems. Meadowlands is a transportable SATCOM system composed of modular Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) / Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) Radio Frequency (RF) monitoring and generation equipment. The design incorporates multi-band antennas and equipment in transit cases. The frequency conversion system (FCS) that handles RF signals between the shelter transit cases to the antenna uses a proprietary photonics system. The system can be transported by C-130 or larger aircraft and by ground transport over improved or semi-improved roads. The system will be designed for operations by trained operators in US-controlled facilities world-wide, and in the Developmental Support Facility (DSF). The Meadowlands �Base Design� system meets current A-spec requirements. All systems have same Transit Case and Antenna configuration/capability. The Meadowlands base design system is comprised of the following major capabilities: Three independent, bidirectional antenna polarization paths Native Support for a single Large Multiband Antenna (LMA) Bands Supported: UHF, L, C, Ku, Ka Two separate independently controlled antenna polarization paths Simultaneous dual polarization operation Receive-only operation if desired Supports Base, and unique network specific missions Native Support for a single 1.2m Antenna Antenna Supports L-Band only The system can operate in three antenna Polarization Paths � Each Polarization Path Contains an Uplink & Downlink RF Interface. The system is capable of simultaneously operating/controlling up to three antennas and associated components utilizing three polarization paths. The Meadowlands system utilizes Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) Ethernet, TCP & UDP/IP Standard interfaces for network communications (Data, Command, Control & Status) between Transit case assemblies, Antennas and the Software Server The Base System Configuration is composed of: 4 System Transit Cases in Shelter (Mission Control & Timing (MCT) Subsystem, Advanced Signal Processor (ASP) Subsystem, Shelter Photonics Unit (SPU1), SPU2) 1 Antenna Transit Case in Shelter for 1.2m Antenna (1.2m Transit Case) 1 Transit Case for Secure External Network Operations (Remote Ops Transit Case) � Contains Firewall & Encryption 2 Transit Cases outside by LMA antenna (Antenna Photonics Unit (APU)2 & APU2) APU Transit Cases The system can operate in the UHF, L, C, Ku, and KA RF Bands for Transmit and Receive via Frequency Conversion System (FCS) The production of the CCS Meadowlands units has been accomplished as part of a Pre-Planned Product Improvement effort. The program utilizes equipment from the CCS Block 10.2 systems as Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) including the LMA Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, High Powered Amplifiers (HPAs), Dummy Loads); the 1.2m Antenna (Including Servo Controller, Feeds, HPAs, Dummy Loads), Power Distribution Units (PDUs) (in transit cases) and also external PDUs, Environmental Control Units (ECUs), Tent, and a Power Management Unit (PMU) Requirements: The market research obtained from this request for information will be used to support a Government decision on the award of additional CCS Meadowlands systems between seven and up to an additional 24 systems. The intent for any future systems to follow the same design and functionality as the existing Meadowlands systems for efficiency in sustainment, training and and maintenance for the operational units. The USG intends to solicit and negotiate a contract or agreement with the contractor that provides the most technically acceptable solution to the USG under the current Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) on the Platform One Solutions Marketplace (P1SM). If interested in pursuing this opportunity, please submit a video to P1SM no later than end of October 2026 to allow time for your submission to be assessed in accordance with the competitive procedures of P1SM. The anticipated period of performance for the resultant award will consist of a 12?month base period and four 12?month option periods. The SI is responsible for planning, executing, and validating integrations between the EM&C platform and external programs/data repositories, including the Joint Management Tool (JMT), Unified Data Library (UDL), EMS Beskar, Blitzar, Protected and Tactical Systems (PATS) Mission Management System, and external commercial/government off-the-shelf software (COTS/GOTS). The SI contractor will not author core application code or dictate enterprise reference architecture. Core application code is developed by designated Development Contractors (DEV), while the architectural roadmap and governance are established by System Engineering & Integration Contractors (SE&I). The SI operates as the technical integrator and operational execution engine thereby, driving Program Increment (PI) planning, deployment automation, release orchestration, and enterprise-level test and evaluation (T&E). The SI must remain strictly independent of core software developers to eliminate any Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI).

description: Since 2010, the ECB implements an environmental management system (EMS) in accordance with the international standard ISO 14001:2015 and Regulation (EC) No 1221/2009, as amended by Regulation (EU) 2017/1505 and 2018/2026. The priority of the ECB remains to prevent greenhouse gas emissions wherever possible, limiting emissions in areas in which they cannot be avoided. The ECB envisages launching a dynamic purchasing system with a duration of initially two years, extendable at the ECB's option by another two years (total duration up to four years).

title: Heavy Equipment Rental Services
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA), the Management and Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy-owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors capable of providing heavy equipment rental services to support laboratory operations at INL facilities in Idaho Falls and at Site locations west of Idaho Falls. BACKGROUND INL utilizes outside vendors to obtain equipment that is unavailable through the Central Facilities Area (CFA) equipment pool or required for specialized tasks. Timely access to safe, compliant, and well-maintained equipment is essential to maintaining project schedules and mitigating risk. Heavy equipment rentals enable BEA to meet operational needs without long-term capital purchases. Proposed base period: January 1, 2027 � December 31, 2027, with four (4) option years extending through December 31, 2031. SCOPE OF WORK Responding vendors must be capable of furnishing heavy equipment rental services on an as-needed basis, including delivery and pickup when requested by BEA. The rental fleet should encompass the following representative, non-limiting categories typically required by BEA, including but not limited to: � Rollers 79-in. & 84-in. double-drum; 84-in. padfoot 12-16 ton class; 84-in. smooth 13-17 ton class; 68-in. pneumatic 14 � 16 ton class � Soil compactors (Heavy-duty, suitable for earthwork and compaction operations.) � Dozers Medium-class with low ground pressure; Medium-class high-track configuration; Large-Class; Extra-large-class � Motor graders Heavy-duty suitable for road construction, maintenance & finish grading) � Excavators and attachments Hydraulic excavators including long-reach 35-ton to 40 ton class, 74-ton class, 90-ton class; Hydraulic Hammer attachments compatible with 36 � 40-ton hydraulic excavator, or 49- to 52-ton hydraulic excavator; Rotary cutters compatible with 36 � 40-ton hydraulic excavator; Multi-processor attachment compatible with 49- to 52-ton hydraulic excavator � Scrapers Heavy-duty self propelled and/or tandem-engine scraper suitable for large-scale earthmoving operations. � Articulated haul trucks (30-ton payload and/or 45-ton payload capacity) � Wheel loaders (Medium-production and/or large-or extra-large production) Fork attachment compatible with the proposed wheel loader; approx. 72-in and 96-in fork lengths � Water equipment (12K gal. watertower, water trucks with 6K gal. and/or 8K gal.) � Rubber track dump trucks (suitable for operation on soft ground or uneven terrain) Equipment furnished shall meet or exceed OSHA, ANSI, and applicable manufacturer maintenance standards; be delivered in safe, good working condition; and include required documentation (inspection records, manuals, tags, capacity charts). PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors for future solicitation. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested firms are requested to provide expressions of interest submitted to chase.egbert@Inl.gov by close-of business on 02 Oct. 2026. Responses must include sufficient written information confirming the responder�s qualifications and interest. Company name and point of contact. NAICS and business size classification Description of rental fleet and capability to supply equipment in the categories listed above, including typical makes/models and availability windows. Delivery and pickup capabilities for INL locations; standard lead times; emergency response capability. Standard equipment delivery timelines should not exceed one-week from the date of request. Repair or replacement of malfunctioning or defective equipment should occur within 24-hours of notification. Maintenance, inspection, and documentation practices; sample service/inspection records. Repair and replacement response commitments (e.g., 24-hour repair/replace) and onsite service coverage. Safety, security, and compliance: confirmation of OSHA/ANSI compliance; onsite requirements (REAL ID; Foreign National Access Program approvals when applicable; BEA escort compliance). Quality program certifications and applicable regulatory compliance (e.g., DOT for transport). Standard rental terms (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly) and pricing structures; discount schedules or IDIQ approaches (note: detailed pricing may be requested in a subsequent RFP). References for similar heavy equipment rental support to government or industrial sites. Note that responses must be no more than fifteen (15) pages in length in PDF format. Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

description: W9123627BA003: Norfolk Harbor Inner Channel to Newport News Maintenance Dredging in Hampton Roads, Virginia This is a pre-solicitation notice. This is NOT a solicitation. It is anticipated that the solicitation will be posted on Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website at https://piee.eb.mil/ by the end of October 2026. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted for 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Norfolk District (NAO) intends to issue an Invitation for Bid (IFB) acquisition for the Norfolk Harbor Inner Channel to Newport News Maintenance Dredging located in Hampton Roads, Virginia. This procurement will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 14, Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government intends to award a firm-fixed-price (FFP) contract. The requirement will be solicited as unrestricted. The applicable NAICS code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction (Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities), with a small business standard of $37 million. In accordance with DFARS 236.204 - Disclosure of the Magnitude of Construction Projects, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The Norfolk District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, is seeking eligible firms capable of performing work that consists of dredging approximately 550,000 cubic yards of maintenance material from the Sewells Point to Lamberts Bend and Entrance Reach Federal navigation channel segments to a required depth of -56 feet MLLW with one foot of allowable paid overdepth. All material will be dredged by mechanical means with the dredged material placed overboard at the Norfolk Ocean Disposal Site. Optional work includes dredging approximately 150,000 cubic yards of maintenance material from the Channel to Newport News and approximately 45,000 cubic yards of maintenance material from the Naval Station Fairway Federal navigation channel segments to required depths of -55 feet MLLW and -47 feet MLLW, respectively, each with one foot of allowable paid overdepth. All optional work maintenance material will be dredged by mechanical means and pumped directly into the cells at the Craney Island Dredged Material Management Area. Contract includes special requirements and precautions when dredging over the Navy Degaussing Array in the Entrance Reach Federal navigation channel segment, and when dredging in the vicinity of protected cultural resources in the Channel to Newport News Federal navigation channel segment. The construction completion date will be approximately 175 calendar days from the issuance of Notice to Proceed (NTP). Contractors will be required to submit bid bonds documents with the proposal. The successful awardee will be required to provide 100% payment and performance bonds for the project. The effort will be solicited and awarded utilizing the Sealed Bid procedures under FAR Part 14. Anticipated solicitation issuance time frame is on or about the end of October 2026. THIS PROJECT IS A FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION PROCUREMENT INVITATION FOR SEALED BID. The Government intends to award a firm fixed price contract using INVITATION FOR BID WITH PRE-AWARD SURVEY and procedures outlined in FAR 36 and FAR 14. Pre-award survey will determine contractor responsibility in accordance with FAR 9.104. Bidders will be evaluated on both pre-award survey and conformance to the solicitation and price. The Government reserves the right to reject any or all Bids; and to award the contract to other than the lowest total price and to award to the bidder submitting the lowest bid determined by the Government to be responsible. Bid bonds will be required with bid submittals. In addition, the awardee must be found responsible in accordance with FAR 9.1. The below Pre-Award Survey Information will be requested of the apparent low offeror. Submit evidence of availability of working/operating capital, which will be used for the performance of the resultant contract. For Joint Venture arrangements, submit the latest three complete fiscal year financial statements for each company in the Joint Venture and discuss the financial responsibilities among the companies. The Government may also utilize Dun & Bradstreet reports to evaluate the financial capacity of the bidder. This notice does not constitute an invitation for bid. The Contractor shall apply engineering competencies to solve complex technical challenges throughout the munition system lifecycle by executing rigorous engineering activities. The Contractor shall apply core engineering disciplines by executing critical technical activities such as performing requirements decomposition and system architecture design; creating detailed Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models; conducting structural, thermal, and kinematic finite element analysis (FEA); designing analog and digital circuit boards; developing embedded software and control algorithms; and formulating developmental test plans alongside post-test data reduction. Through these tasks, the Contractor shall deliver engineering artifacts such as Interface Control Documents (ICDs), Technical Data Packages (TDPs), simulation reports, and software version descriptions and actively participate in formal/informal reviews to ensure robust engineering rigor, standard methodologies, and scientific discipline are applied to the development, production, and sustainment of the munition systems. They will review designs and Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) against military and commercial specifications, Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) standards, and producibility standards and proactively identifying opportunities to reduce costs, accelerate schedules, optimize manufacturing processes, and elevate overall quality. Throughout the life cycle, the contractor shall be responsible for supporting project preparation encompassing planning, cost analysis, scheduling, facility coordination, and integration. description: This sole-source justification provides authority to award a task order on the basis of other than full and open competition for Systems Engineering and Technical Assistance (SETA) support services. The contractor will perform SETA services to assist the SC Security Technology Integration Program (STIP) in system development and operations and maintenance (O&M). This includes providing technical guidance throughout the acquisition lifecycle and systems engineering life cycle (SELC), reviewing open architecture (OA), System of Systems (SoS), design documentation, and supporting risk management activities. The contractor will also assist in developing and maintaining documentation, reviewing operational processes for compliance and efficiency, supporting incident response and troubleshooting, and execution of major initiatives within STIP and related security technology efforts. These services will ensure accurate reporting and device connectivity to TSANetwork (TSANet) via the Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) for alarm counts and throughput data. The contractor will validate the accuracy and integrity of system-generated reports, support improvements to reporting tools, and ensure compliance with Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and TSA data standards. Additionally, the contractor will review and validate device integration with TSANet, verify data transmission protocols, and assist in resolving connectivity issues to ensure reliable data collection and aggregation. STIP is the interface of Secure Flight (SF), Credential Authentication Technology CAT 2 (CAT-2), enhanced metal detectors (EMDs), and connectivity of other Transportation Security Equipment (TSE). These TSEs enhance the capabilities necessary to sustain TSA�s mission-critical operations, equip the frontline, and safeguard the traveling public. STIP provides the connection between TSEs located in airports and the TSANet for sharing of mission, and operational and maintenance data. Specifically, STIP enables network connectivity for exchanging the near-real time passenger vetting status of more than 1.7 million passengers daily between TSA�s SF system and over 2,100 CAT / CAT-2 units deployed at airports across the country. Without a STIP connection, that data cannot be shared with the checkpoints and data is performed manually by Transportation Security Officers (TSOs) on an hourly basis. SETA support services are paramount to providing technical monitoring of the STIP platform including analysis of vulnerabilities to the system and identification of process improvements and efficiencies to current and continuous operational changes. Only B&B can provide the required continuity of services with the highest level of confidence while maintaining support for active and time-sensitive SC initiatives and operations and maintenance services. These SC initiatives include ensuring successful management and completion of Advanced Imaging Technology (AIT) connectivity, Security Technology Information eXchange (STIX) connectivity, and operational utility evaluation (OUE) activities by November 2026; ensuring successful management and completion of the STIP database server migration to Windows Server 19 by January 2027; ensuring successful completion and operational readiness of the Data Center 15 (DC15) development lab by March 2027; and ensuring successful management and completion of ongoing STIP engineering change requests (ECRs), enhancements, and O&M. +++++++++++++

title: Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot
description: Diffuusiokapasiteetti/Spirometrialaitteistot Hankinnan kohteena on Etelä-Savon hyvinvointialueen (Eloisa) Mikkelin keskussairaalaan tuleva diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteisto (1 kpl) sekä laitekohtaiset kulutustarvikkeet, ohjelmisto, lisenssit ja huoltopalvelu. Hankinnassa on lisäksi optio kahdelle (2) vastaavanlaiselle laitekokonaisuudelle (diffuusiokapasiteetti-/spirometrialaitteistot) sekä yhdelle (1) spirometrialaitteistolle. Eloisa päättää mahdollisten optioiden hankkimisesta vuoden 2028 loppuun mennessä. Sopimuskausi alkaa sopimuksen allekirjoittamisesta. Sopimus allekirjoitetaan mahdollisimman pian lainvoimaisen päätöksen jälkeen. Sopimus on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva. Laitteen tulee soveltua diffuusiokapasiteetin mittaamiseen ja spirometriatutkimusten tekemiseen. Spirometria ja diffuusiokapasiteetti ovat keskeisiä keuhkojen toimintakokeita. Spirometrialla mitataan keuhkojen tilavuutta ja ilman virtausta, mikä auttaa tunnistamaan ahtauttavat (esim. astma, COPD) tai rajoittavat keuhkosairaudet. Diffuusiokapasiteetti mittaa kaasujen siirtymistä keuhkorakkuloista vereen, ja sitä käytetään keuhkokudoksen sairauksien (esim. fibroosi) arvioinnissa. Laitteella tulee pystyä tekemään spirometria ja bronkodilataatiokoe, diffuusiokoe hengityslihasvoiman mittaus sekä SNIP. Pyydettäessä tarjoaja toimittaa kustannuksellaan tarjotun laitteistokokonaisuuden koekäyttöön Mikkelin keskussairaalalle. Tarjouspyyntö julkaistaan ehdollisena optioiden osalta: optioiden hankinnat voidaan toteuttaa, mikäli hankinnoille varatut investointimäärärahat hyväksytään.,

description: 1. Purpose The Department of War (DoW) is conducting market research to identify interested and capable businesses that can provide test pilot training in support of the US Air Force Security Assistance Training (AFSAT) squadron. Anticipated Mandatory Institutional Accreditations, Approvals, and Credentials The Government anticipates that a future solicitation may require the successful contractor to maintain the following institutional accreditations, approvals, and credentials. Συνοπτικά το αντικείμενο περιλαμβάνει σύμφωνα με τους όρους του συνόλου των συμβατικών τευχών: Α1) Την εκπόνηση της Μελέτης. Α5) Την σύνταξη και υποβολή των τευχών τεκμηρίωσης, των εγχειριδίων συντήρησης και λειτουργίας και των εικονογραφημένων καταλόγων ανταλλακτικών. Α6) Την εκπαίδευση του προσωπικού της ΣΤΑΣΥ. Α1 έως Α6, ποσό εκατόν έξι εκατομμύρια πεντακόσιες χιλιάδες Ευρώ (106.500.000€) χωρίς ΦΠΑ. Β) Για τα ανωτέρω υπ’ αρίθμ. title: Germany – General management consultancy services – Beratungsleistungen zur Konzeption und Einführung eines integrierten Unternehmenssteuerungssystems
description: Die Verwaltungsdirektion des WDR beabsichtigt, einen Rahmenvertrag über Beratungs-, Konzeptions- und fachliche Begleitleistungen für das Projekt "Business Warehouse" abzuschließen. Das Vorhaben ist als mehrjähriges Transformations- und Umsetzungsprojekt angelegt. Ziel des Projekts ist die fachliche Konzeption und schrittweise Einführung eines integrierten Steuerungsmodells, das strategische Planung, Mittelallokation, Portfolio- und Performancebetrachtung sowie Transparenz über Ressourcen, Kosten und Wirkung miteinander verknüpft. Das Vorhaben dient damit der Weiterentwicklung der unternehmensweiten Steuerungsfähigkeit des WDR. Der Auftragnehmer begleitet das Vorhaben von der Feinkonzeption über die Umsetzungsphase bis zur Produktivsetzung und dem Übergang in den Regelbetrieb. Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung sind ausschließlich Beratungsleistungen, die fachliche Konzeption sowie die fachliche Begleitung des Projekts über alle Projektphasen hinweg. Erwartet wird auch die fachliche Konzeption und Begleitung der technischen Umsetzung sowie die Übersetzung fachlicher Anforderungen in umsetzbare Prozess-, Daten- und Systemanforderungen. Die technische Implementierung und Softwareentwicklung selbst sind nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Der Auftrag wird als Rahmenvertrag ohne Abnahmeverpflichtung ausgeschrieben. Die Vertragslaufzeit beträgt 27 Monate ab Leistungsbeginn; der WDR erhält die Option, den Ver-trag einmalig um ein weiteres Jahr zu verlängern. Die geschätzte Abrufmenge beträgt ca. 350 Personentage; die Höchstmenge beträgt 400 Personentage. Mit Erreichen der Höchstmenge endet die Möglichkeit weiterer Abrufe aus dem Rahmenvertrag. Aus der geschätzten Abrufmenge folgt keine Verpflichtung des WDR, Leistungen in diesem Umfang abzurufen.
